method: Verified identical supplied exam bytes against the previously extracted and visually inspected final exam. Screened every revised stem, option and feedback for new 12-word overlap, and compared tasks qualitatively. Q1–8 and Q22–28/Q30 calibrate ordinary application, causal chains, numerical-graph integration and stabilization; Q29 and Q31–40 set monetary/Phillips boundaries.
limitation: Lexical overlap is a screening aid, not proof. Existing library assets are retained; no exam image, option pattern or scenario was imported. The Hard multiplier graph task adds an explicit total offset and separates reference-price demand from equilibrium GDP, rather than simply revaluing the exam example.

items.humanComparison: Uses the existing library graph or selected mechanism with original offset definitions, inverse constraints, timing or evidence-identification reasoning. The exam supplied cognitive calibration rather than an item template.
